Global sum.text: Global sum Sum the entire matrix. This is effective when enough signal accumulates across all affected entries. Time complexity: . Its mean under the alternative is .

Exhaustive scan.text: Exhaustive scan Search for the row and column subsets whose standardized sum is largest. The search can detect more localized signals but is combinatorial. Time complexity: . The candidate blocks can be searched exactly by enumerating row sets and sorting column sums.

Column pooling.text: Column pooling Sum each column across rows, then test whether any pooled column is unusually large. This preserves signals in tall, narrow blocks. Time complexity: . An affected column has mean after pooling.

Maximum entry.text: Maximum entry Reject when an individual entry is unusually large. This is the matrix analogue of a minimum-p-value test: it does not use the shared block structure. Time complexity: . Ma and Wu (2015) show sufficient detection when .

Combined sum and scan.text: Combined sum and scan Reject whenever either the global sum or exhaustive scan rejects. This combines the two regimes without weakening the statistical exponent boundary. Time complexity: exhaustive scan dominates. The two component thresholds should be chosen jointly to control the desired false-positive rate.

Exhaustive block maximization.text: Exhaustive block maximization Keep the maximizing row and column subsets from the scan rather than only the maximum value. Butucea, Ingster and Suslina (2015) establish a sharp boundary for exact recovery. Time complexity: for direct enumeration. Optimal statistically at sufficient signal, but combinatorial.

Spectral projection.text: Spectral projection Use the top left and right singular vectors to form row and column scores. Their separation identifies the affected indices without enumerating candidate blocks. Time complexity: polynomial; per dense power iteration. For , Cai, Liang and Rakhlin (2017) give success when .

Thresholded spectral projection.text: Thresholded spectral projection Soft-threshold the matrix entries before computing singular vectors, reducing the influence of noise when the planted block is smaller. Time complexity: polynomial, with thresholding followed by spectral iterations. For , their theorem gives success when .
